title: handle() has match ($action) with no default. If an action passes checkAction() but has no arm, what is thrown?
explain: match without a matching arm throws UnhandledMatchError. It is an Error, not a FileServiceException, so the user gets 500. Today it cannot happen, because ACTION_METHODS and the match have the same actions. But these are two lists: add 'rename' to one and forget the other, and you get a 500.

title: getStatusCode() uses match (true) with instanceof. B extends A. What does this print?
explain: match (true) takes the FIRST arm that is true. B is also an A, so the A arm wins. In her code each exception extends FileServiceException directly, so the order does not matter yet. If one day FileNotFoundException extends StorageException, put the more specific class first.

title: Senior asks: why is FileServiceException abstract?
options: Nobody can throw the general one: every error must say what it is (not found, storage, invalid…)
explain: You can still catch FileServiceException (the controller does), but you cannot throw it directly. That forces a specific class, and each class has its own HTTP code in getStatusCode().

title: Senior asks: why does FileServiceException extend RuntimeException and not LogicException?
options: These errors come from the outside world (files, user input), not from a bug in the code
explain: LogicException means 'the code is wrong, fix the code' (for example a wrong argument from another class). RuntimeException means 'something outside went wrong at run time': a missing file, a full disk, bad user data. File processing errors are the second kind.

title: CsvFileActions::read() checks headers with array_unique. Header is id,fruit,id. What does this print?
explain: array_unique removes the second 'id', so the counts differ and read() throws 'Column names must be unique.'. Why it matters: array_combine() would silently keep only the last 'id' column, and data would be lost.

title: The page sends [] for write to fruits.csv by mistake. What happens?
options: The file is saved empty: all fruits are gone
explain: write() accepts an empty list: no headers, no rows, so saveContent() writes an empty file. The old data is lost, with a '200 saved' answer. A senior may ask for a guard: refuse an empty list, or keep a backup before overwrite.

title: In FileNameResolver::createEmptyFile(), why is file_exists() checked again after fopen() fails?
options: A mistake, it can be removed
To tell 'someone took this name' (try the next) from 'cannot write at all' (throw), so the loop never runs forever
explain: fopen('x') returns false in two cases: the name was taken a moment ago, or the folder is not writable. If the file now exists, try name_1, name_2…. If not, writing is impossible, so throw StorageException. Without that check, a read-only folder would make the while loop endless.

title: MAX_UPLOAD_SIZE is 1 MB. Someone uploads a 50 MB file. What does the user most likely see?
options: File is too big. Maximum size is 1 MB.
explain: PHP checks post_max_size (often 8 MB, 2 MB in some setups) before your code runs. If the request is bigger, PHP drops the body, $request->files is empty, and the controller says 'No file uploaded.'. The 1 MB check only works for files below the PHP limit. Fix the limits in php.ini too, and check UploadedFile::getError() for a clear message.

title: Senior asks: why is declare(strict_types=1) in every file?
options: It is set once for the project
It works per file: each file decides how its own calls convert types
explain: strict_types is per file, for the calls written in that file. One file without it would silently turn '5' into 5 again. Having it everywhere means wrong types fail early with a TypeError.

title: Senior asks: JsonDecodeTrait is used in FileController and JsonFileActions. Trait or small class?
options: A trait copies code into both classes; a small JsonDecoder class could be injected, mocked and tested alone
explain: For one tiny helper a trait is OK and short. But a trait adds hidden methods to a class and cannot be replaced in a test. If the JSON rules grow (error messages, depth, big numbers), a JsonDecoder service is easier to test and change in one place.

title: DELETE action called with GET returns 405. What does the HTTP standard also expect in that answer?
options: An Allow header with the allowed method
explain: A 405 response should say what is allowed: Allow: DELETE. Tools and browsers can read it. Her MethodNotAllowedException already knows the expected method, so adding the header is small.

title: Uploading notes.txt returns 400 today. Which code describes it more exactly?
explain: 400 means 'your request is wrong' in general. 415 says exactly: this format is not supported. Small detail, but a senior notices when the codes tell the client what to fix.

title: public/.htaccess sends unknown paths to index.php. Does composer serve (php -S) use it?
options: No: .htaccess is for Apache only; php -S ignores it
explain: .htaccess works only on Apache with mod_rewrite. The built-in PHP server ignores it, so locally you always call index.php?action=… directly. On nginx you would need a try_files rule instead.

title: Senior asks: why is Composer\Config::disableProcessTimeout in the serve script?
options: Composer stops scripts after 300 seconds; a dev server must run longer
explain: Composer kills any script that runs longer than process-timeout (300 s). php -S runs until you stop it, so without this line the server would die after 5 minutes.

title: Senior asks: why only symfony/http-foundation and not the full Symfony framework?
options: The app needs only Request/Response: one small package, no framework rules or config
The framework does not support PHP 8.4
http-foundation is free, the framework is paid
explain: Symfony is made of separate components. For a tiny API, one component gives the HTTP objects without routing, DI container and config. If the project grows (routes, services, forms), moving to the full framework is the next step.

title: You test uploads locally and run git status. What do you see, and why?
options: Your uploaded test files in storage/: .gitignore ignores only vendor/ and caches
explain: storage/ is tracked because it has the sample files. Every test upload appears as a new file, easy to commit by mistake. Option: ignore storage/* but keep the samples with !storage/fruits.csv, or move samples to a fixtures folder.

title: Senior asks: make FileService final. What breaks?
options: FileControllerTest: createMock(FileService::class) cannot mock a final class
explain: PHPUnit makes mocks by extending the class, so final classes cannot be mocked. That is a hint: the controller should depend on an interface (FileServiceInterface), then FileService can be final and the test mocks the interface.

title: uploadFile() calls $(this).val('') right after reading the file. Why?
options: To delete the file on the server
So choosing the same file again fires 'change' again
explain: A file input fires change only when the value changes. If the user uploads fruits.csv, fixes it and picks fruits.csv again, nothing would happen. Clearing the value makes every pick a change.

title: app.js shows file names with $('<option>').text(fileName). Why not .append('<option>' + fileName + '</option>')?
options: text() inserts plain text: a file named .csv cannot run code
append does not work with select
explain: File names come from users (upload). String HTML would run any HTML inside the name: XSS. .text() and .attr() escape it. She did it right everywhere: messages also use .text().

title: getErrorMessage(xhr) falls back to 'Something went wrong.'. When is xhr.responseJSON missing?
options: When the answer is not JSON: a PHP fatal error page, a proxy error, no connection
explain: Her API always answers JSON, even on 500. But a PHP fatal error before the try, a 502 from a proxy, or a lost connection give HTML or nothing. The fallback keeps the page working in those cases.

pr.title: Add Allow header to 405 answers
pr.author: senior-reviewer
pr.body: HTTP says a 405 must list the allowed methods.

explain: Good change: clients and tools see which method to use. It needs a small getter in MethodNotAllowedException that returns the expected method from its constructor.

pr.title: Do not save an empty CSV
pr.author: senior-reviewer
pr.body: A wrong click sent [] and wiped fruits.csv.

explain: Good change. Overwriting a file with nothing is almost always a mistake, and the old data cannot be recovered. A clear 422 is better than a silent '200 saved'. (If deleting all rows is a real use case, add an explicit action for it.)

pr.title: Remove ACTION_METHODS, use match only
pr.author: senior-reviewer
pr.body: Two lists of actions are hard to keep in sync.

explain: The goal is right, but the PR drops the method check: DELETE via GET would work again, and a link or a crawler could delete files. Keep one list that holds both the method and the handler.
